name: Political Science
overview: Political Science is the study of governments, political processes, policies, and the behavior of individuals and institutions within societies. It examines power distribution, decision-making processes, and how political systems shape domestic and global affairs, drawing from history, sociology, economics, law, and international relations. The field offers careers across government, diplomacy, policy research, academia, NGOs, and international organizations, enabling professionals to influence governance and address societal challenges.

topJobs.description: Analyzes political systems, government structures, policies, and international relations through research and data interpretation for universities, think tanks, or government bodies.
Examines political trends, elections, and government policies to provide strategic guidance and forecasts to political parties, NGOs, and international organizations.
Represents their country abroad, managing international relations, promoting national interests, and fostering political, economic, and cultural cooperation.
Manages government programs, policies, and public services across health, education, infrastructure, and social welfare sectors.

institutesInternational: London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) (UK)
careerLadder: High school foundation in political studies, history, economics, and current affairs
Undergraduate degree in Political Science, International Relations, Public Policy, or Governance
Internships/trainee roles in government, embassies, think tanks, or NGOs
Master's degree in Political Science, International Relations, or Public Administration
Professional roles as Political Scientist, Analyst, Diplomat, or Public Administrator
Advanced certifications in public policy, diplomacy, or governance
Ph.D. in Political Science or International Relations (for research/academic paths)
Senior positions as Ambassador, Director, Senior Policy Advisor, or University Professor
